How much a result depends on the open band's assumed cap

Source: R/bands.R, R/print_boxes.R
bandsens.Rd

Recomputes a statistic of banded data (by default the Gini coefficient) for a range of assumed caps on the open top band, and reports how far the answer moves. Every statistic computed from banded data depends on where the open band is assumed to end; this function measures that dependence, so you can report a range instead of a single figure when the dependence is large.

Usage

bandsens(bands, cnts, stat = ginicoef, caps = NULL, rule = "midpoint")

# S3 method for class 'rmbl_band_sensitivity'
format(x, digits = 4L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rmbl_band_sensitivity'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

bands

A data frame from prsbands, or labels to parse.

cnts

Numeric vector, one per band: how many units fall in each band. Non-integer counts are truncated by rep().

stat

A function that takes a numeric vector of per-unit values and returns one number. Default ginicoef.

caps

Numeric vector of caps to try, in the units of the labels. Default NULL: the geometric sweep described in Details. Values are sorted and de-duplicated.

rule

Character, default "midpoint": the placement rule passed to bandvals.

x

An rmbl_band_sensitivity object.

digits

Significant digits of the printed numbers.

...

Further arguments to print(); the band table ignores them.

Value

A data frame of class c("rmbl_band_sensitivity", "data.frame") with numeric columns cap and value, and attributes span, relspan and base (the lower bound \(b\) of the open band).

Details

Let \(b\) be the smallest lower bound among the open top bands. The default caps are 12 points spaced evenly on the log scale from \(1.05 b\) to \(20 b\). For each cap \(c\), bandvals(bands, rule, openupcap = c) gives one value per band, each value is repeated cnts times, and stat is applied to the result. A statistic that errors or does not return a single number gives NA; warnings are suppressed.

The span is \(\max - \min\) over the finite values and the relative span is the span divided by the median absolute value (NA when any value is zero). The print method adds a note when the relative span exceeds 0.1.

Errors: cnts not numeric or of a different length from the bands; no open top band.

Examples

b <- prsbands(c("1", "2 to 5", "6 to 10", "Greater than 10"))
counts <- c(1200, 430, 110, 38)

s <- bandsens(b, counts)
s
#> ╭── Sensitivity to the open top band's assumed cap ───────────────────────╮
#> │   Open band starts at         11                                        │
#> │   Caps tried                  12                                        │
#> │   Span over the caps          0.2747                                    │
#> │   Share of the typical value  53.7%                                     │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │      cap   value                                                        │
#> │   ------  ------                                                        │
#> │    11.55  0.4255                                                        │
#> │    15.10  0.4346                                                        │
#> │    19.74  0.4461                                                        │
#> │    25.80  0.4604                                                        │
#> │    33.73  0.4780                                                        │
#> │    44.09  0.4993                                                        │
#> │    57.63  0.5245                                                        │
#> │    75.34  0.5538                                                        │
#> │    98.49  0.5868                                                        │
#> │   128.74  0.6229                                                        │
#> │   168.30  0.6611                                                        │
#> │   220.00  0.7002                                                        │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   span over the caps tried: 0.2747 (53.7% of the typical value). The    │
#> │   statistic moves by more than a tenth of itself across the caps tried, │
#> │   so it is a property of the assumption as much as of the data. Report  │
#> │   the range, not a single figure.                                       │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
attr(s, "relspan")
#> [1] 0.5366908

# A statistic that barely moves has been measured; one that swings
# has not.
bandsens(b, counts, stat = mean, caps = c(12, 20, 50))
#> ╭── Sensitivity to the open top band's assumed cap ───────────────────────╮
#> │   Open band starts at         11                                        │
#> │   Caps tried                  3                                         │
#> │   Span over the caps          0.4061                                    │
#> │   Share of the typical value  17.3%                                     │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   cap  value                                                            │
#> │   ---  -----                                                            │
#> │    12  2.262                                                            │
#> │    20  2.348                                                            │
#> │    50  2.668                                                            │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   span over the caps tried: 0.4061 (17.3% of the typical value). The    │
#> │   statistic moves by more than a tenth of itself across the caps tried, │
#> │   so it is a property of the assumption as much as of the data. Report  │
#> │   the range, not a single figure.                                       │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# nothing to vary without an open band
try(bandsens(c("1", "2 to 5"), c(10, 4)))
#> Error : no open upper band, so there is nothing to be sensitive to
